paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates a comparison of loss with respect to training time for two models, identified as Vanilla and SepLLM. The x-axis, labeled "Training Time (s)", utilizes a linear scale ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds, with tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 50,000. The y-axis, labeled "Loss", employs a linear scale ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, features no specified units, and displays tick marks at regular intervals of 0.05. The "Vanilla" model is represented by a solid purple line with upward-pointing triangle markers, which exhibits a continuous decline across the x-axis, starting at a loss slightly above 2.75 near 20,000 seconds and ending precisely at a loss of 2.50 at 250,000 seconds. The "SepLLM" model is depicted by a solid red line with circular markers, demonstrating a similar continuous decline; it begins at a loss of approximately 2.71 near 15,000 seconds and terminates at roughly 2.49 near 235,000 seconds. Additionally, the plot features a horizontal green dashed line at a loss value of 2.50, intersected by both the red and purple lines. Vertical green dashed lines drop down to the x-axis from these two intersection points—at approximately 195,000 seconds for SepLLM and exactly 250,000 seconds for Vanilla—which are highlighted with green star markers. A green double-headed arrow spans the horizontal gap between these two vertical lines, accompanied by the text "1.26×".
